request.brief: Design a single supplier digest preferences screen for someone setting the cadence of their supplier digest. The only choices are Daily, Weekly, and Off. Weekly is selected initially, with Monday selected. The day-of-week control appears only for Weekly. Saving shows a clear local confirmation of the saved frequency and, for Weekly, its day. Prioritize quick scanning, an obvious selected state, accessible controls, and a quiet, assured and distinctive visual identity. It must work at Chrome widths of 1440 and 390 pixels. The output is a single self-contained HTML document, with original inline artwork or CSS visuals, Google Fonts permitted, and no other remote assets. Use only these facts. There is no brand, supplier list, account data, sending time, or schedule history to show. Keep copy brief and give the form one visual focal point tied to delivery cadence.

Create a distinctive, clear reading preferences screen for a cooking app, for a home cook who wants a comfortable, quick-to-scan recipe step while working in the kitchen. The entire product content is a title, Text size with Standard and Large, Line spacing with Comfortable and Compact, a live sample with precisely 'Rest dough for 20 minutes.', and a clear reset to Standard and Comfortable. Initial settings are Standard and Comfortable. Design for Chrome at 1440 px and 390 px, with accessible native controls, intentional typography, strong selected states, and a deliberate responsive structure. Output will be one standalone HTML file, inline CSS/JS, optional Google Fonts, and original inline vector or CSS detail. Seek a composed cookbook colophon or editorial index feeling with a restrained kitchen-specific focal detail that leaves room for the live text. Pick concrete typography, colors and composition grounded in one source. No additional product features or copy beyond helpful labels.
avoid: large decorative hero competing with the settings
